label: sparse conjunction: early original-phase token shortly after u/p/j (necessary-ish context only)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.04% of steps). About 84% of mass is in the original phase at t=3..6 (peak t=3), and the input one or two steps back is usually u, p or j (u gives about 10x lift). Weaker preferences: current input x/m/f/3, first token x/3/c/o. A small remainder (about 16%) is in the copy phase, mostly at recall_idx 1 and 5..7. It does not fire at t=0..1 and almost never at the delimiter. Magnitude is narrow (median 0.12, max 0.21). The top examples have u at position 2 or 3 followed by f/m. The context predicate gets about 76% of mass but under 1% precision; adding token conditions raises precision only to about 8% and costs most of the recall. So the feature looks like a conjunction of several token identities that no simple predicate captures.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=x (+7.95), phase=2 & out_tok=x (+4.08), prev2_tok=p (+3.50), prev_tok=p (+3.35), orig0=x (+3.24), prev_tok=u (+2.96). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-6.45), in_tok=j (-3.35), recall_idx=4 (-3.31), in_tok=p (-3.22).
